title: Antibodies after hepatitis B vaccine (anti-HBs)
what: This blood test shows how many protective antibodies to hepatitis B you have after the vaccine.
why: For health workers, people on dialysis, family of people with hepatitis B, and people with a weak immune system, to see if the vaccine worked.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: When you had your last hepatitis B shot
How many shots you had in total
If you had hepatitis B before
If you recently had a blood transfusion or immunoglobulin

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The test is usually done 1 to 2 months after the last shot in the series. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast strictly, but it is better to come 3 to 4 hours after a light, non-fatty meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
If antibodies are low, the doctor may offer another shot
Keep the result with your vaccination records
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.a: The lab form shows the protection threshold. If your result is above it, the vaccine worked.

faq.q: Does everyone need an antibody check after the vaccine?
faq.a: No. It is usually checked in people at high risk of infection. Your doctor will advise.

reminders.text: Hepatitis B antibody test tomorrow. Bring your vaccination records.
